visual_system:
TYPOGRAPHY: Almost everything is set in one neo-grotesque, 'Helvetica Reg' (a self-hosted HelveticaNeueLTStd-Roman.otf), with a single handwritten script, 'Quickpen' (a Trial-by-Cupcakes font), used only for the hero greeting 'Hello Gorgeous!'. The script is 58px desktop / 36px mobile, bold, white, with a soft text-shadow (.04em .04em .12em rgba(0,0,0,.18)). Body copy is 16px/1.7 (27.2px) Helvetica in mid-gray #585858, weight 500. Section headings are small and quiet: 22-24px Helvetica bold, #565656, 1px letter-spacing, sentence case (for example 'The Secret to Healthy, Beautiful Hair'). Page-banner H1s are 36-40px ALL CAPS white Helvetica with a drop shadow, centered on a photo strip ('OUR SERVICES', 'MEET YOUR STYLIST'). The main nav is 13-14px Helvetica ALL CAPS with no tracking, in near-black rgba(0,0,0,.6). The utility bar uses Open Sans 12px semibold ALL CAPS in #565656. Buttons use Inter 14px ALL CAPS. Services category headers are the heaviest type on the site: about 26px black extended/bold ALL CAPS ('COLOR', 'CUT & STYLE') with a 1px rule on each side. Stylist-page names are about 32px ALL CAPS gray, with a role label like 'S T Y L I S T' in 13px caps at about 0.3em tracking.

COLOR: The logo, utility bar and footer band use one saturated lemon yellow, #FFE800, which is about 5-8% of the page area. Neutrals do most of the work: white page, charcoal #565656 for buttons and card labels, #2A2A2A footer, light gray #EDEDED panels. Yellow also appears in the salon photos (the giant yellow 'e' disc on the reception desk and the wall sign), so photography and brand color reinforce each other. Yellow is the hover state for every button (charcoal or ghost to #FFE800 with dark text, 0.3s transition). Only one button on the home page is yellow at rest: 'BOOK AN APPOINTMENT' above the footer.

SPACING/GRID: Divi 1080px content column (180px side margins at 1440). The two exceptions are the home feature-card row and the 4-up look-book strip, which run wider (~1296px). Sections are fairly tight, with 20-60px vertical padding, so density is medium-high and the page reads more like a brochure than an editorial site. Layouts are standard 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3 cards, 4-up image rows, and 40/60 image-plus-text splits alternating sides.

GRAPHIC DEVICES: (1) A 'brushed silver' diagonal gradient behind alternating sections: linear-gradient(154deg, #606060 0, rgba(225,225,225,.11) 35%, rgba(96,96,96,.39) 100%). It gives a metallic, salon-mirror sheen. (2) Heavy soft drop shadows on buttons and card labels (5px 5px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.3)) with a 0.8px white border and square 0px corners. (3) A yellow map-pin icon in the footer location columns. (4) Dotted leader lines on the price menu.

IMAGERY: Two distinct treatments. Team headshots are all shot in the same session against the same backdrop (a mirrored herringbone tile wall with light streaks). They are converted to high-contrast black and white and cropped square, 1:1, 225-320px. Everything else is bright, natural-light color documentary photography of stylists working (foils, blow-drys, Bellami wefts) at about 1.41:1 (400x284 thumbs) or 3:4 portrait. Client results appear as 4 portrait 4:5 tiles (295x369) of finished hair from Instagram. The hero is a full-width muted, looping MP4 of the storefront 'element' sign. It is only 385px tall on desktop (not full viewport) with a dark overlay, and full-width about 390px tall on mobile. Inner pages use a 220px-tall photo banner strip with a centered caps title.

MOTION: Divi fade-in on scroll (et_animated) for images and rows, 0.3s color/background transitions on buttons, a card label that turns #C4C4C4 on hover, and a fixed header that shrinks from ~138px to ~84px (logo shrinks from ~85px to 50px) while the yellow utility bar stays pinned above it.
navigation:
DESKTOP: The header has two tiers, both fixed on scroll. Tier 1 is a 35px lemon-yellow (#FFE800) utility bar, right-aligned, Open Sans 12px semibold caps in #565656: SUSTAINABILITY · LOOK BOOK (opens Instagram) · PROMOTIONS · MEET YOUR STYLIST · SHOP ONLINE · an envelope icon (mailto). Tier 2 is a white bar, logo left (yellow circle 'e' over 'element salon' in light gray lowercase Helvetica), links right in 14px caps: TEAM & LOCATIONS ▾ (Green Hills / Brentwood / Elliston / All Team) · ABOUT · SERVICES · EXTENSIONS · JOIN OUR TEAM ▾ (Apply Now / Our Culture / Core Values). The last item is a filled charcoal #565656 'BOOK NOW' button with white caps and a drop shadow. On scroll the white bar shrinks to ~84px with a 1px 1px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.1) shadow. BOOK NOW stays visible, and the yellow bar stays pinned too. The active page shows as lighter gray text; there is no underline. Location is a primary nav concept (a multi-location group), and recruiting ('Join Our Team') gets top-level space, which a client-facing salon would normally demote.

MOBILE: An 80px white header with a small logo left and a hamburger right. There is no visible Book button and no phone icon in the header. Tapping opens a Divi dropdown panel, a white card below the header, that lists the full primary nav with submenus already expanded, then a small charcoal BOOK NOW button about 7th-8th in the list, then the utility links (Sustainability, Look Book, Promotions, Meet Your Stylist, Shop Online, Email). The yellow utility bar is hidden on mobile. There is no sticky bottom booking bar. A floating reCAPTCHA badge sits bottom-right.

PERSISTENT CTAs: Only the header BOOK NOW on desktop. Otherwise CTAs repeat inside content: in the hero, as the third feature card, mid-page, and a yellow button above the footer. Every service line item has its own 'BOOK NOW →' link.
home_flow:
1) YELLOW UTILITY BAR + STICKY WHITE NAV with a charcoal BOOK NOW button. This sets the brand color immediately.
2) HERO, 1440x385: a muted looping video of the storefront 'element' sign under a dark overlay, with the script 'Hello Gorgeous!' (58px Quickpen) and two stacked ghost buttons with a 1px white border: 'BOOK AN APPOINTMENT' and 'NEW TO ELEMENT? WE'D LOVE TO MEET YOU!'. The second button opens a popup with an embedded Phorest 'Request a Call Back' consultation form. The same popup is set to fire on exit intent (class 'popup on-exit'). This splits returning clients (book) from new clients (talk to us first) in the first viewport. The H1 'Element Salon Nashville' is hidden: 2px, transparent, SEO-only.
3) ONE-LINE POSITIONING: 'Discover Nashville's premier destination for exceptional stylists and expert haircare.' (24px centered).
4) THREE FEATURE CARDS (photo + charcoal label bar with white caps title and subline): MEET YOUR STYLIST ('Find a stylist for you'), ONLINE STORE ('Shop Kerastase, Shu Uemura & more'), BOOK NOW ('Schedule an appointment'). These are three intent-based doors: match me, buy product, book. The label bars sit over the bottom of each photo with a heavy shadow.
5) SOCIAL PROOF: centered H2 'Named top 100 salons in the country by Elle Magazine 4 years in a row!' plus a paragraph ending with the catchphrase 'Hello, Gorgeous!'.
6) EXPERTISE SPLIT on a brushed-silver gradient: a portrait of a colorist foiling (left), then 'The best stylists and haircare experts in Nashville call Element Salon home.', copy naming the specialties (balayage, dimensional color, extensions, smoothing), and two charcoal buttons: SERVICES and LUXURY EXTENSIONS. This routes into the two big-ticket categories.
7) RESULTS STRIP: 4 portrait 4:5 photos of finished hair (lived-in balayage, platinum bob, copper, blonde). No captions or stylist credit.
8) PRODUCT PHILOSOPHY: 'The Secret to Healthy, Beautiful Hair' (partnering with the best haircare brands) plus a BOOK NOW button.
9) RECRUITING SPLIT on silver gradient: a salon interior with the yellow 'e' desk, then 'Join Our Team' and APPLY NOW.
10) LOCATIONS: 'Visit Our Hair Salons in Nashville, TN'. Three location blurbs (Green Hills / Brentwood / Elliston), each with a one-line specialty hook and MORE INFO, next to a Google Maps embed of Elliston only.
11) LOCAL-SEO FAQ ACCORDION for Elliston on a silver gradient: location, Bellami extensions, how to book, services, parking. It uses white/light-gray accordion rows with a ⊕ icon, then 'Serving Midtown, Music Row, West End…', then the only yellow-filled button at rest, 'BOOK AN APPOINTMENT'.
12) FOOTER: a #2A2A2A band with 3 location columns (yellow pin icon, caps name, address, phone, ghost MORE INFO), then a yellow band with round black social icons and the copyright, then a gray 'Powered by Blueprint.Inc' band.

Conversion logic: book-first hero with a soft-lead alternative, then three intent doors, then proof, specialties, results, and location/FAQ, closing on a book CTA. The weak spots are that recruiting interrupts the client journey and that results have no attribution.
services:
WEBSITE MENU (/services/): Opens with a 220px photo banner titled 'OUR SERVICES', then an honest pricing disclaimer: 'Prices will vary depending on the stylist. During the consultation your stylist will go over your beauty budget and what the cost will be before your service begins… a valid credit card is required to secure your appointment.'

The menu is a restaurant-style price list in 2-column panels: COLOR | CUT & STYLE, then TREATMENTS | EXTENSIONS. Each panel's background is a salon photo washed out to about 85% white, so the imagery reads as texture behind the text. Each category header is a heavy black ALL-CAPS word centered between two 1px horizontal rules, with a small right-aligned 'STARTING AT' label under it. Each line item reads: bold name, dotted leader, bold price right-aligned, a 2-4 line plain-language description, and a small gray 'BOOK NOW →' text link. Example: 'Base Color ........ $124 / During a base color, your colorist will apply color to the root area of your hair to cover grey or blend regrowth up to 3 inches / BOOK NOW →'. Treatments include practical specs like 'In salon treatment time: 3 hrs; Durability: Approximately 56 shampoos (about 16 weeks). May shampoo hair 72 hours after…'.

Prices: Base Color $124, Balayage $155, Partial Highlight $155, Full Highlight $176, Gloss '$' (blank), Clipper/Pixie $42, Medium/Long Haircut $63, Transformation Haircut $84, Keratin Complex $336, Express Keratin $140, Kerastase Fusio-Dose $40, Mask $12. Extensions carry no prices. They get a long educational column (Bellami, Tape-Ins, I-Tips, K-Tips, Hand-Tied Wefts), each with 'Application & Aftercare' notes, and a named list of extension specialists by location.

EXTENSIONS PAGE (/luxury-hair-extensions/): A split hero (right-aligned 'Luxury Hair Extensions' at about 48px, 'Transform your look.', copy, and a large Bellami install photo). Next come 4 method descriptions (Tape-In, Hand-Tied/Volume Wefts, K-Tip, I-Tip) and a dark photo band 'Why Choose Us?' (Bellami Pro certified). The band notes that every extension service starts with a consultation, and its CTA is 'BOOK YOUR EXTENSION CONSULTATION'. Last is an 'Extension Information' matrix: three cards (Green Hills / Brentwood / Elliston Place) with charcoal headers, each listing stylists and the methods they do (for example 'Marissa: Sew-ins, Tape-ins, K-tips, I-tips'), with linked names and a BOOK NOW per location.

IN THE BOOKING TOOL (Phorest): Categories are Add On, Color, Color Finishing Services, Extensions, Haircut & Styling, Smoother, Treatments, each with a count badge. Each service is a white shadowed card showing 'from $171.00' and a radio button. Some booking prices don't match the site (Full Highlight is $176 on the site but from $171 in Phorest; Partial Highlight is $155 vs $150). No filtering exists on the website itself. There are no durations on the site menu apart from the treatments, and no tier or level pricing is explained, even though stylists are tiered in Phorest.
stylist_credibility:
TEAM PAGE (/team/): It opens with 'TEAM', an intro, and anchor links 'Green Hills | Brentwood | Elliston'. Leadership comes first: 3 larger 320px square B&W portraits with name plus title (Director of Operations, Director of Marketing, Director of New Talent). Then per-location sections with caps headers (GREEN HILLS / BRENTWOOD / ELLISTON), each a 4-up grid of 225px square B&W headshots with first name only, centered, in 16px bold gray. The strongest asset is that every headshot comes from the same studio session against the same mirrored herringbone wall, graded to high-contrast B&W. Thirty-plus stylists read as one polished, cohesive team, and a new hire slots in seamlessly. One stylist still shows a gray silhouette placeholder ('photocomingsoon.jpg'). Location pages reuse the same grid, so each salon's page shows its own team.

INDIVIDUAL STYLIST PAGE (/team/kate-hartnett/): light gray #EDEDED panel. The left side holds a 396px square B&W portrait. The right side has the full name in caps (~32px), a spaced-caps role 'S T Y L I S T', a bold one-line hook ('With her attention to detail, Kate will make you look and feel like a star.'), a 4-paragraph narrative bio (origin, experience, specialties, philosophy, and her role as an educator/mentor), a round Instagram icon linking to the stylist's personal IG, and a charcoal BOOK NOW. Some profiles add a specialty line ('Master Stylist • Balayage x Color Specialist'), but others say 'Bio coming soon.'

Missing: no portfolio or gallery of the stylist's own work, no level or price tier, no location label, no specialties tags, no reviews, and BOOK NOW goes to the generic /book-now/ location picker instead of deep-linking to that stylist in Phorest.

STYLIST LEVELS exist only inside Phorest's Staff tab (Level 1, 2, 3, 4, 4A, 4AA), and they drive the 'prices vary by stylist' pricing, but the website never explains them.

MATCHMAKING: The Meet Your Stylist page ('Find your perfect stylist with our matchmaking survey!') offers 3 location buttons that launch a Mya quiz, a branded multi-step flow with a segmented progress bar. The questions are: services wanted (Haircut / Hair Color / Hair Extensions / Hairstyling / Formal), hair type (Curly, High Texture, Thick & Coarse, Fine & Thin, Fine but a lot of it, Thinning), hair challenges (Frizz, Dry, Damaged, Oily…), and current style (Long Layers / Mid-Length / Pixie / Bob), then match results. Below the buttons is a 4-column gallery of about 28 behind-the-scenes color photos of stylists working, which gives a documentary sense of craft.

OTHER CREDIBILITY: The Extensions matrix names the specialists per method. The About page shows a photo of the L'Oréal 'Top 100 Salon' trophies, and Our Culture cites L'Oréal Top 100 out of about 25,000 accounts, monthly education, 6-hour shifts, and benefits.
booking_ux:
PLATFORM: Phorest, run as separate accounts per location (elementsalonbrentwood, etc.). Booking entry points:
(1) The header BOOK NOW on every page.
(2) The hero 'BOOK AN APPOINTMENT'.
(3) The 'BOOK NOW / Schedule an appointment' feature card.
(4) Mid-page and closing 'BOOK NOW' / 'BOOK AN APPOINTMENT' buttons.
(5) A per-item 'BOOK NOW →' under every service on /services/.
(6) Location pages (BOOK NOW + GIFT CARD outline buttons).
(7) Stylist pages (BOOK NOW).
(8) Extensions 'BOOK YOUR EXTENSION CONSULTATION' plus per-location BOOK NOW.
Every one of these goes to the same /book-now/ page. None carries a service, stylist or location parameter.

FLOW:
/book-now/ shows a 'BOOK AN APPOINTMENT' heading and a sales sentence, then an embedded Phorest iframe (elementsalonbrentwood.phorest.me/locations) titled 'Select a location', with 3 location rows (green pin icon, name, street). In our desktop capture the iframe rendered squeezed into a very narrow column, one word per line, which looks broken.
Choosing a location leaves the site for phorest.com/salon/<location>. That is a Phorest landing page in an unrelated olive/khaki brand color with 'Welcome to Element Salon', a location dropdown, and three buttons: 'Make an Appointment >' / 'Visit our Shop' / 'Buy a Gift Card'. It also shows 'Book a call back', address, phone and email.
'Make an Appointment' opens /book/service-selection: a Services | Staff segmented toggle, 'Search for service', and accordion categories with count badges. Expanded, a category shows 2-column white cards like 'Balayage - Full   from $171.00 ○'. The Staff tab lists stylists with round avatars and 'Level 2' / 'Level 4A' labels.
That is 3 clicks minimum before choosing a service, across 2 domains and 2 visual brands.

NEW-CLIENT FLOW: The hero button 'NEW TO ELEMENT? WE'D LOVE TO MEET YOU!' opens an on-page popup, which also fires on exit intent, containing Phorest's 'Request a Call Back' consultation form. Fields: first/last name, mobile phone with a country selector, email, 'Tell us more about your needs and how we can help', 'Do you have a location preference?' dropdown, preferred contact (Phone/Email radio, Phone pre-selected), and a marketing email/SMS consent checkbox that is pre-checked, then Submit. The popup's iframe points at a Phorest account named 'elementsaloneastnashville', which doesn't match any current location. The Mya matchmaking quiz is a second new-client path.

MICROCOPY: 'Hello Gorgeous!' as the brand greeting, 'New to Element? We'd love to meet you!', 'Find a stylist for you', 'Schedule an appointment', 'Book Your Extension Consultation', and 'Please note that a valid credit card is required to secure your appointment.' (card-on-file policy stated up front on the services page).

GIFT CARDS: There is no gift-card link in the nav or footer. The only on-site entry is the GIFT CARD button on location pages, and on Green Hills and Brentwood its href is empty (broken). Elliston links to gift-cards.phorest.com. Otherwise gift cards are only reachable inside Phorest. SHOP ONLINE links out to Phorest short links per location.
signature_moves: Consistent B&W studio headshots as a team system: every stylist is shot in one session against the same textured backdrop (here a mirrored herringbone wall with light streaks), converted to high-contrast black and white and cropped square, shown 4-up with first name only. This makes a large, mixed team look curated and premium, and new hires blend in. Reproduce with one photo day, a single backdrop and a CSS grid of 1:1 images (aspect-ratio:1; object-fit:cover).

Two front doors in the hero: a primary 'Book an Appointment' next to a warmer secondary 'New to [Salon]? We'd love to meet you!' that opens a short consultation/call-back form (name, phone, email, needs, preferred location, preferred contact method). Returning clients go straight to booking; nervous first-timers get a human first. Keep the marketing opt-in unchecked by default.

Stylist matchmaking quiz: a 'Meet Your Stylist, find your perfect stylist with our matchmaking survey' page with a 4-6 step, one-question-per-screen flow and a segmented progress bar (services wanted, then hair type: Curly / Thick & Coarse / Fine & Thin / Fine but a lot of it, then challenges: frizz, damage, dryness, then current style), ending in recommended stylists. It can be built as a lightweight multi-step HTML form with option chips that maps answers to stylist specialty tags.

Restaurant-style price menu: a heavy ALL-CAPS category word centered between two hairline rules, a tiny right-aligned 'STARTING AT' label, and rows of bold service name, dotted leader, bold price, a 2-3 line plain-English description, and a small 'BOOK NOW →' text link. Category panels sit on a salon photo washed to about 85% white. Adding practical specs to treatments ('In-salon time 3 hrs · lasts ~16 weeks · wait 72 hrs to shampoo') builds trust.

Specialist matrix for a complex category: for extensions (or a spa's specialty services), a 3-column card grid by location with dark header bars, listing each specialist by name plus the exact methods they do ('Marissa: Sew-ins, Tape-ins, K-tips, I-tips'), each name linked to their profile, with a Book button per card. It answers 'who can do this?' at a glance.

One saturated brand color used sparingly as a frame: lemon yellow (#FFE800) only on the logo mark, a thin 35px utility bar on top, the footer social band, and every button's hover state (charcoal to yellow with dark text). Everything else is white / #565656 / #2A2A2A, and the same color shows up physically in the salon photos (the yellow 'e' disc on the reception desk). For Bellezza, pick one signature accent and let the interior photography echo it.

Script greeting as a brand voice: a single handwritten-script line ('Hello Gorgeous!') over the hero video, repeated as the sign-off of body copy. A plain grotesque does everything else. One personal flourish against a neutral system is memorable without looking templated.

Three intent cards right under the hero (photo with an overlapping dark label bar, caps title plus a small subline): 'Meet Your Stylist: Find a stylist for you' / 'Online Store: Shop Kerastase…' / 'Book Now: Schedule an appointment'. These are clear doors for the three main reasons people visit, each a full clickable card with a shadow and a label that changes on hover.
weaknesses: Booking breaks the brand: every Book button lands on one generic /book-now/ page with a narrow, cramped Phorest iframe (text wrapping one word per line in our capture). The flow then jumps to phorest.com in an unrelated olive/khaki palette and needs 3+ clicks (location, then 'Make an Appointment', then category) before a service is picked. No button passes a service, stylist or location, so the per-service 'BOOK NOW →' links and stylist-page Book buttons don't pre-select anything.

Mobile has no persistent booking CTA: the header is just logo plus hamburger, BOOK NOW is buried about 7th in an expanded dropdown list below the 'Join Our Team' submenu, there is no sticky bottom bar or tap-to-call, and a reCAPTCHA badge covers the bottom-right corner.

Price and content inconsistencies hurt trust: the site says Full Highlight $176 while booking says from $171, and Partial Highlight $155 vs $150. Gloss is listed as '$' with no number. The awards claim reads '4 years in a row' in the H2 but 'three consecutive years' in the paragraph under it, and the About page's trophies are L'Oréal awards, not ELLE. The FAQ gives a placeholder phone '(615) 555-1234'. The services page lists specialists at a '12 South' location that no longer appears anywhere else.

Stylist levels (Level 1-4AA) drive 'prices vary by stylist' but are shown only inside Phorest. The website never explains tiers or price ranges per level, and stylist profiles have no portfolio, level, specialties tags, reviews, or location label. Some bios say 'Bio coming soon', and one headshot is a gray silhouette placeholder.

Broken or dead items: the GIFT CARD button on the Green Hills and Brentwood pages has an empty href, gift cards aren't in the nav or footer (a missed revenue path for a salon/spa), 'Promotions' is a top-bar link to a page that says 'Check back for information about our next promotion', and 'Look Book' just jumps to Instagram.

Visual bugs and generic Divi look: the Elliston card on the home page renders gray text on a gray block (unreadable), only one of three locations gets a map, the hero H1 is hidden (2px transparent text) for SEO, headings are small (22-24px) and gray so the hierarchy is flat, and the heavy drop shadows on square charcoal buttons read dated and templated rather than luxe.

Recruiting ('Join Our Team', Apply Now, Our Culture, Core Values) takes top-level nav and a full home-page section, which interrupts the client conversion path. The About page is keyword-stuffed SEO copy ('best hair salon in Nashville' repeated) rather than a story.

The new-client consultation popup also fires on exit intent, embeds a Phorest form tied to a defunct 'eastnashville' account, pre-selects Phone as contact method, and pre-checks marketing SMS/email consent.

The About page has an olive stat-tile row alternating with photos ('15 Licences & Certifications', '25+ Years') and a floor-by-floor tour ('First Floor / Second Floor / Basement' panels, each with a 3x2 gallery and a stat pair), plus a cream '360 tour' band with a full-bleed panoramic still. weaknesses: No real online booking: every 'Book' CTA either scrolls to a request form at the bottom of the page or goes to a WooCommerce checkout. No availability is shown, no instant confirmation is given, and paying for a service still leaves the time unscheduled.

Mobile has no sticky Book/Call bar, the reCAPTCHA badge covers the bottom-right corner, blog thumbnails disappear and leave big empty gaps, and the form is extremely long.

Many QA and copy errors: 'Alma Lassers'; the ClearLift block labelled '[Massages]'; the hair 'Cut' section described with Shellac manicure copy; duplicate head spa rows (#4 and #5); the gift card shown twice in a 3-card carousel; a 'MISSING IMAGE' placeholder in the Shop; 'We has over 800 variety of color selections'.

One sans family in two weights, sized in big jumps (62/42/24/16), with plain sentence-case eyebrows, reads more like a generic template than luxury. The home page has no H1 (the hero title is an H2), which hurts SEO and accessibility.

visual_system:
TYPOGRAPHY. There are three families.
(1) Display is Arsenal Regular, a flared humanist sans with calligraphic stroke endings that reads like Optima. It is always weight 400 and nearly always all caps with wide tracking of about 0.1em. Measured sizes: 'WE'RE HIRING' 49px/1.3 with 4.9px tracking; 'THE ARTISTS' 38px with 3.8px; services category heads 'COLOR / HAIRCUT / TREATMENTS' 28px with 4.2px (0.15em), centered; 'MEET THE ARTISTS' 28px with 2.8px plus a 40px x 2px rule under it; 'FROM OUR CLIENTS' 24px with 2.4px. Two page titles break the all-caps rule and are set larger in title case with normal tracking: 'SAY HELLO' at 56px/1.4 and 'ABOUT / US' at about 56px, stacked and right-aligned.
(2) UI and labels use Hanken Grotesk, a geometric grotesk. Nav is 13px with 2.6px tracking (0.2em), caps, bone on taupe. Phone and address in the utility area are 12px with 1.8px (0.15em). Buttons are 14px weight 700 with 1.4px (0.1em). Service item names are 15px/700 with 0.1em tracking, caps; service group labels ('TINTS', 'HIGHLIGHTS') are 17px/700. Stylist names are 20px/400 with 3px (0.15em), caps. Stylist roles are 13px lowercase with 1.95px tracking ('owner & colorist'). Contact kickers are 14px with 2.1px, in taupe. Footer copyright is 11px with 1.1px tracking.
(3) Body is Noto Sans. General text is 14px with a very airy 26.6px line-height (1.9) and 0.7px (0.05em) tracking. The hero lede is 18px/32.4px (1.8). Service descriptions are 14px.
Hierarchy comes from tracking, case and the switch between Arsenal and Hanken, not from weight. There is no bold display type anywhere.

COLOR. Four colors do almost all the work: taupe-umber #5D564B (sticky nav bar, footer, button borders and hover fill, form Send button); bone #F4F3F2 (text on taupe, flat page grounds); charcoal #414141 (all body text, never pure black); and one saturated accent, chestnut brown #754E36. The chestnut appears only on tiny UI: carousel dots, the round chat bubble, and Mangomint's selected-step pill and 'Continue' button. Footer muted text is #837E73. Stylist portraits add a warm cognac/caramel backdrop (about #8B5A2B to #A0672F) that doubles as a brand color. Photography is warm and low-key: olive greens from palm fronds, dark wood, black leather chairs, cream walls, and a slightly underexposed, desaturated grade with crushed shadows. Rough proportion: 75% textured grey-bone ground, 15% photography, 10% taupe.

GROUND AND TEXTURE. Page backgrounds are photos, not flat fills. Home and About sit on a fixed, full-viewport photo of a warm grey plaster wall with a soft diagonal patch of window light (position:fixed, 1440x900, object-fit:cover), so content scrolls over a stationary 'room'. Services and Careers use a white plaster texture with blurred palm-leaf shadows. Gallery and Policies drop back to flat #F4F3F2.

SPACING AND GRID. Density is low. The home page is only about 3,190px tall across 4 content blocks. Section gaps run 100 to 170px. The stylist grid has about 170px of vertical gap between rows. Text measures are narrow (about 380px for the Artists paragraph, about 650px for reviews). Columns are asymmetric: the hero text column starts at x=186 while two 375x681 portrait images sit at x=597 and x=1019 (47px gutter, 46px right margin); Artists pairs a 640x692 photo at x=80 with text at x=840. The stylist grid uses two 443x431 near-square cards at x=234 and x=763 (86px gutter). The gallery is a bento of alternating rows: 433+867px, then 867+433px, all 613px tall with 10px gutters.

IMAGERY. Everything is framed, not full-bleed. The hero uses two tall portrait crops (about 0.55 ratio, close to 9:16) of the salon interior: a chair against palm fronds, and a coffee-table still life. The group team photo is darkened. The 'We're hiring' band is inset about 77px from each side (1286x500) and uses a sticky image inside the frame for a reveal parallax, plus a dark overlay. The 'Ready to schedule?' band on Services is full-bleed at 500px tall. The gallery is interiors and still life only (books, incense, shampoo bowls, combs), with no hair results.

GRAPHIC DEVICES. A 1px vertical hairline divider recurs: in the logo 'THE LANE | S/F' (S and F stacked small after the rule), in the 'ABOUT | US' heading (right-aligned heading, 2px vertical rule, then paragraph), and in the nav label 'ABOUT | ARTISTS'. Short 40px horizontal rules separate a quote from its attribution. On the Services page, 1px charcoal full-width rules sit under each group label.

BUTTONS AND LINKS. Ghost pills: 1px #5D564B border, 30px radius, 44px tall (146 to 205px wide), 14px bold caps with 0.1em tracking plus a chevron glyph. On hover the button fills solid #5D564B with bone text over a 0.2s transition. On dark photos the border and text are bone. The only solid button on the whole site is Book Now in the mobile drawer (filled taupe pill). Nav hover and active state is an underline. Contact form fields are underline-only (1px bottom border) with a full-width taupe rectangular 'Send' button.

MOTION. Restrained: a fixed background, the sticky-image parallax inside inset bands, a slow fade on the testimonial carousel, and hover fills. No scroll-triggered reveals were observed.

DESKTOP. Two tiers, and only the top tier is sticky.
Tier 1 is a 41px taupe (#5D564B) bar, sticky at the top (header height 54px). It holds seven links spread evenly across the full 1440px width: HOME, ABOUT | ARTISTS, SERVICES, GALLERY, SALON POLICIES, CAREERS, CONTACT, in 13px Hanken caps with 0.2em tracking, bone on taupe. The current page is underlined. There are no dropdowns.
Tier 2 scrolls away with the page and sits on the textured ground (about 104px tall). On the left is the 283x56 logo lockup 'THE LANE | S/F'. On the right is a right-aligned stack: phone '(415)780-0806' as a tel link, then '1821 STEINER ST. SAN FRANCISCO, CA', both 12px caps with 0.15em tracking. Beside the stack is a ghost pill 'BOOK NOW ›' (146x44) linking to Mangomint in the same tab.
Consequence: once you scroll, Book Now is gone. The sticky bar carries no booking CTA and no phone number.

MOBILE. The site renders Wix's separate 320px mobile layout, scaled up. The header is the logo left and a thin three-line hamburger right. There is no visible Book Now or phone, and the header does not stay on screen when scrolling. The hamburger opens a right-side drawer about 70% of screen width, with the textured wall photo as its ground and a dim overlay on the page. The drawer has a small stacked logo ('| THE / LANE'), a close X, right-aligned 16px caps links spaced about 58px apart, and a filled taupe pill 'BOOK NOW' (about 170x52) at the bottom of the list. A chestnut circular chat bubble (60px) floats bottom-right on every page and every viewport, and on mobile it overlaps content such as stylist role labels.

FOOTER (identical on all pages). Solid taupe band about 285px tall, centered: bone 'THE LANE' wordmark, address in 12px caps with 0.15em tracking, phone, Yelp and Instagram glyph icons, and an 11px copyright plus designer credit. There are no footer nav links, no hours, no map and no newsletter signup.
home_flow:
1. HERO (y=147 to 979, one viewport). There is no headline or H1. On the left, bottom-aligned with the photos, sits a 3-line lede in Noto 18px/1.8: 'A clean beauty salon / specializing in precision / haircuts and custom color.' Under it is a ghost pill 'SERVICES ›'. On the right are two tall 375x681 portrait photos of the interior (a salon chair against palm fronds, a coffee table with art books), both over the fixed wall-texture ground. Conversion role: set the mood and point to the menu. It is positioning by atmosphere, not an offer. The only booking CTA is the small header pill.
2. THE ARTISTS (y=979 to 1726). A 640x692 darkened group photo of the team on the left. On the right, vertically centered: 'THE ARTISTS' (Arsenal 38px), a 6-line paragraph naming the husband-and-wife owners Frank and Stevie Lane and calling the team 'precision haircut and color specialists', and a ghost pill 'MEET OUR TEAM ›'. Role: people-first trust, showing a named, owner-operated shop rather than a faceless brand.
3. FROM OUR CLIENTS (y=1726 to 2305). A carousel of 6 long, specific Google reviews, each naming a stylist ('Frank', 'Ali', 'Lindsey'), in centered 14px Noto about 650px wide. A 40px rule, then 'NAME | GOOGLE REVIEW' where 'GOOGLE REVIEW' links out to the Google reviews panel. Chestnut dot pagination and thin line chevrons pinned to the viewport edges. Role: social proof that also sells individual stylists.
4. WE'RE HIRING (y=2305 to 2855). An inset 1286x500 band with a sticky-image parallax of the salon floor, a dark overlay, 'WE'RE HIRING' in Arsenal 49px bone, and a bone ghost pill 'JOIN OUR TEAM ›'. Role: recruiting, placed in the slot most salons would use for the final booking CTA.
5. FOOTER (taupe; address, phone, Yelp, Instagram).
Net effect: the page runs on mood and trust, but the body has no booking CTA at all. The final full-width band recruits staff instead of asking the visitor to book.
services:
SITE SERVICES PAGE (/services, about 2,440px). A plain text menu on a white-plaster texture, with no photos and almost no prices.
- Structure: centered Arsenal 28px category heads with 0.15em tracking (COLOR, HAIRCUT, TREATMENTS). Under COLOR are left-aligned group labels (TINTS, HIGHLIGHTS) in Hanken 17px bold caps, each followed by a 1px full-width rule.
- Items sit in a two-column grid inside a 1060px measure (x=190 to 1250). Each item is a name in Hanken 15px bold caps with 0.1em tracking, plus an optional one-line Noto 14px description ('Color applied roots to ends of hair', 'Soft grey blending', 'Maintenance appointment').
- Items: Tint (all over), Regrowth only tint (maintenance), Men's tint, Virgin bleached base & color, Bleached regrowth with toner, Toner with blowdry; Highlight, Touch up highlight, Mini highlight; Haircut, Blowdry; OWay Smoothing Treatment ($450, 'anti-frizz, lasting 3-5 months'), Milbon Gold Deep Conditioning Treatment.
- Only one price is shown anywhere on the page ($450). There are no durations and no 'from' prices. Casing is inconsistent ('OWay', 'Milbon Gold' in mixed case).
- The page ends in a full-bleed 500px photo band of the salon interior with 'READY TO SCHEDULE?' in Arsenal about 49px bone and a bone ghost 'BOOK NOW ›' pill.

REAL PRICING appears only inside the Mangomint widget. It is grouped as an accordion: HAIRCUTS (Haircut $175+, Bangs or fringe refresh, Neck cut $50), STYLING (Blow Dry $100+, New Client Bang trim $60), COLOR (Highlight balayage or foil $425+, Touch up highlight $350+, Tint with highlight $525+, Tint with touch up highlight $425+, Tint regrowth $200+, Tint all over $225+, Men's grey blending $125+, Bleached regrowth with toner $425+, Virgin bleached base with toner $600+, Toner with blow dry $150+) and TREATMENTS. Some rows have a 'more info' expander.
Pricing is tiered per stylist rather than by a named level system. After choosing Haircut, the stylist list shows each person's own price: Lindsey $175, David $185, Ali $195, Lacey $200, Chris $200, Frank $260, Todd $275. 'Anyone' shows the range $175–$275. There is no filtering, no service photography, and no dedicated page per category.
stylist_credibility:
TEAM PAGE (/about-artists). It opens with the split heading 'ABOUT | US' (about 56px, right-aligned, 2px vertical rule) next to a paragraph on Pacific Heights location, owner-operators and values. A 1356x383 inset image band follows, then 'MEET THE ARTISTS' (Arsenal 28px plus a short rule).
Eleven stylists are shown in a 2-up grid of 443x431 near-square portraits with 86px gutters and about 170px between rows. The photography is the strongest asset: every person is shot three-quarter or full length, standing, in their own clothes, against the same cognac/caramel seamless paper backdrop, with the same soft key light and warm grade. The consistency makes eleven different people read as one brand.
Under each photo, on one baseline: the name on the left (Hanken 20px caps, 0.15em tracking) and the role on the right (13px lowercase tracked: 'owner & colorist', 'owner & stylist', 'stylist', 'colorist').
Missing: bios, specialties, years of experience, level or price tier, Instagram handles, portfolio of their work, and any 'Book with [name]' link. Cards have no hover state and are not clickable.
Credibility is carried instead by (a) the owners named on home and About; (b) Google reviews that name individual stylists, shown in a carousel on home and on About, where it sits over a full-bleed darkened interior photo; and (c) the Mangomint stylist picker, which reuses the same cognac portraits as round avatars and adds each stylist's working days (e.g. 'TUE-SAT') and personal price. That picker is the most informative stylist view on the whole site.
booking_ux:
PLATFORM. Mangomint (https://booking.mangomint.com/879391). It opens in the same tab (target _self) as a centered white card about 500px wide on a #F8F8F8 ground. The card header shows The Lane logo with 'POWERED BY mangomint'. The brand accent is chestnut #754E36 for the step pill and the primary button.

ENTRY POINTS.
1. Desktop header ghost pill 'BOOK NOW ›'. It scrolls away and is not in the sticky bar.
2. The 'READY TO SCHEDULE? / BOOK NOW' photo band at the bottom of Services.
3. Contact page copy: 'Ready to book an appointment? Click here.' (italic underlined link).
4. Mobile drawer: filled taupe 'BOOK NOW' pill, which is the only booking entry on mobile and needs a hamburger tap first.
5. Phone tel links in the header and footer ('give us a call or text').
The home page body has no booking CTA.

FLOW, as walked:
1. 'Select a service:' with a blush strip 'Visited us before? Rebook a past service' (one-tap rebook for returning clients), then an accordion of HAIRCUTS / STYLING / COLOR / TREATMENTS showing prices as '$175+'.
2. Service summary ('Haircut, Change, $175 - $275'), then an add-on upsell: 'Milbon Gold Treatment, Deep Hydration or Protein Replenishment, + $100' with a round + toggle, then a full-width chestnut 'Continue'.
3. Stylist picker: an 'Anyone' row (group icon, MON-SAT, $175 - $275), then each stylist with a round cognac avatar, name, working days in tiny caps, and a personal price aligned right.
4. 'Your service: Haircut with Anyone, Remove. Do you want to add another service? Yes / No'.
5. Date step: a 'September / October 2026' week strip of 7 days (unavailable days greyed, selected day in a filled chestnut circle), a blush 'Selected Date: Thursday, October 1, 2026' bar, slots grouped by daypart in an expandable row ('AFTERNOON: 1:00 PM - 2:30 PM'), outlined slot buttons, and 'Not seeing a time that works for you? Join our waitlist'.
6. Confirm: a recap panel (date, 'Haircut ($175 - $275) at 1:00 pm'), phone first, then first/last name and email, an 'I am booking for someone else' toggle, comments, the full 48-hour / 100% cancellation policy text with an 'I agree' checkbox, separate yes/no radios for reminders and for marketing SMS, then 'Book Now'.
A breadcrumb pill (Back › Service › Date › Confirm › Success) tracks progress. No account or password is required. Per the site policy, a card must be on file (collected at or after confirmation).

NEW CLIENTS. There is no new-client page or first-visit guidance. The only cue is a 'New Client Bang trim $60' service under STYLING. Policies (card on file, 48-hour cancellation with 100% charge, no dogs, parking at the Japantown garage plus a map) live on a separate Salon Policies page linked from primary nav.

GIFT CARDS. None. There is no gift card page or link anywhere on the site.

MICROCOPY is friendly and understated: 'Ready to schedule?', 'Say hello / We would love to hear from you', 'Questions? Fill out the form, or give us a call or text.'
signature_moves: Photographic page ground instead of flat white: a full-viewport photo of a warm plaster wall with soft window light or blurred palm shadows, fixed behind the content (position:fixed; inset:0; object-fit:cover; z-index:-1, or background-attachment:fixed), so every section floats over a 'real room'. Use a different texture per page family (a warm-grey light patch for home and about, white plaster with leaf shadow for the service menu) and keep text charcoal #414141, never black.

Two-tier header where the top tier is a thin (about 40px) solid umber strip (#5D564B) holding caps nav at 13px with 0.2em tracking, spread edge to edge with justify-content:space-between. Below it is a roomier logo row: logo left, then a right-aligned stack of phone and address in 12px caps with 0.15em tracking, next to a ghost pill. Borrow the look, but put Book Now inside the sticky strip; The Lane's biggest miss is that it scrolls away.

Vertical-hairline lockup as a brand device: 'THE LANE | S/F' (a 1px rule, then the two city letters stacked small), reused as a split page title. Set the heading right-aligned in about 56px humanist display, add a 2px vertical rule, then a 14px/1.9 paragraph to its right. Also reused as the nav label 'ABOUT | ARTISTS'. Easy to reproduce with CSS grid (auto 2px 1fr).

Ghost pill buttons with a chevron: 1px umber border, border-radius 30px, height 44px, 14px bold grotesk caps with 0.1em tracking, and a '›' glyph. On hover the pill fills solid umber with bone (#F4F3F2) text over a 0.2s transition. Reserve a solid fill for the single most important CTA (The Lane fills only the mobile-drawer Book Now).

Uniform stylist portrait system: every team member shot three-quarter length, standing, in their own clothes, against the same cognac/caramel seamless backdrop with the same light and grade. Shown as near-square cards in a 2-up grid with very generous row gaps (about 170px). Under each image, on one baseline: the name in tracked caps on the left and a lowercase tracked role ('owner & colorist') on the right. Reuse the same crops as round avatars in the booking step. The shared backdrop color becomes a brand color.

Headline-less editorial hero: two tall portrait (about 9:16) photos of the space set side by side in the right 60% of the viewport with a 47px gutter, and a 3-line 18px lede plus one ghost pill bottom-aligned in the left column. Mood over messaging; it feels like a magazine spread rather than a template banner.

Inset 'window' CTA bands: a photo band inset about 5% from each side (e.g. 1286x500 at 1440 wide) with the image position:sticky inside its clipping frame for a reveal parallax, a dark overlay, one line of widely tracked display caps (about 49px, 0.1em) and a bone ghost pill centered. Used for 'READY TO SCHEDULE?' and 'WE'RE HIRING'.

Stylist-specific transparency in booking: the stylist step lists 'Anyone' with the price range ($175–$275, MON-SAT), then each stylist with avatar, working days (TUE-SAT) and their own price. Add a 'Visited us before? Rebook a past service' shortcut strip above the menu and a single add-on upsell card before date selection. All of this can be mirrored on a static site as a 'price by stylist' table and on stylist cards.
weaknesses: Book Now is not persistent. On desktop only the thin nav strip is sticky, and it has no booking button or phone. On mobile the header has no Book Now at all (it hides inside the hamburger drawer) and the header does not stay on screen.

The home page body has zero booking CTAs. The hero button goes to Services, the next goes to the team page, and the final full-width band is a recruiting ad ('We're hiring') in the slot usually reserved for the closing booking CTA.

The services page shows almost no prices (one of about 14 items), no durations and no 'from' prices. Real pricing ($175+ haircut, $425+ highlight, per-stylist $175–$275) is only discoverable by starting a booking.

Stylist cards have no bios, specialties, experience, level or price tier, Instagram, portfolio, or 'Book with [name]' link. The cards are not clickable, even though the booking engine already knows each stylist's price and days.
The gallery is interiors and still lifes only, with no haircut or color results and no before/after, so it builds atmosphere but not proof of skill.
No gift cards, no new-client page or FAQ, no hours anywhere on the site (days appear only per stylist in booking), and no footer navigation, map or newsletter signup.
Primary nav spends two of seven slots on SALON POLICIES and CAREERS, while revenue items (gift cards, book, pricing) are absent. Policies could live in the footer or the booking flow.

Wix's 320px mobile layout is scaled up, so tap targets and text are small. The floating chat bubble covers content such as stylist role labels. There is no H1 on the home page (hurts SEO), text on the footer is low-contrast (#837E73 on #5D564B), and service-name casing is inconsistent ('OWay', 'Milbon Gold').
